h1:
Takua Pa Old Town
Sino-Portuguese shophouses on a quiet old street
intro: Takua Pa was once a busy tin-mining trade port — its old name was Takkola — and it did well for itself in its day. Chinese, Dutch, Portuguese, and British traders came here to do business, and when the price of tin fell the foreign merchants moved on. But the Chinese community stayed and blended into southern Thai life, leaving behind a stretch of two-storey Sino-Portuguese shophouses you can still see today. If you're based around Khao Lak and want to swap the beach for a different mood for half a day, this is the place to do it.

blocks.html: A lot of people get confused about which day the market in Takua Pa Old Town runs, so let's clear that up first. There are two different times people come here. The first is the morning market, which sells food every day from around 4am into the late morning — the real deal that locals actually eat at. The other is the Sunday evening walking street on Si Takua Pa Road, which has been running since 2007 and only opens on Sunday evenings, roughly 3pm–8pm (busiest in high season, Nov–Apr). If you want both the morning food and the walking-street atmosphere, Sunday is the day that gives you the most.

blocks.text: The Sino-Portuguese shophouses and photo spots

blocks.html: The heart of the old town runs along Si Takua Pa Road — rows of two-storey shophouses with arched doorways, painted in pastels, with stucco detailing that mixes Chinese and European styles. Walk it slowly and you can photograph the whole street. The old-town stretch is about 500 metres, an easy walk with no need to rush.

items.name: Baan Khun In
items.blurb: A soft-green Sino-Portuguese house and one of the most popular photo spots in the old town. The architecture is still in great shape.

items.name: Tao Ming School
items.blurb: An old building in pale eggshell yellow that speaks to the Chinese community's roots in Takua Pa. A classic angle that's easy to frame.

items.name: TROK Cafe
items.blurb: A cafe set inside the shell of an old building right in the old town, open only on Sundays to match the walking street. Sip a coffee and take in the architecture.

items.name: Bun Sung Iron Bridge
items.blurb: An old iron bridge across the Takua Pa River, not far from the old-town quarter. Quiet, with a lovely atmosphere for photos in the evening.

blocks.title: Photo tip
blocks.html: Morning light before 9am and the hour near dusk are when the shophouses look their best — midday sun is harsh and hot. If you come on a Sunday evening, the crowds start building after 3pm, so if you want photos of an empty street, get there early.

blocks.text: The old-town morning market — what to eat

blocks.html: The Takua Pa morning market is the kind of legendary local food scene that locals genuinely eat at. Plenty of stalls open before dawn and sell out fast, so if you're set on the famous ones, come before 8am. Here are the spots people around here recommend.

items.name: Pa Lan's Old-Style Khanom Buang
items.blurb: Khanom buang made to an old recipe, with the batter ground in-house from rice and fresh coconut. The result is thick and soft, different from the usual crispy version — and it sells out very fast.

items.name: Jin Keng
items.blurb: Dim sum, pork dumplings, pa thong ko, and kaya custard in the Chinese-Takua Pa style. Opens very early and runs into the late morning — a good spot for a proper sit-down breakfast.

items.name: Ko Chai Mee Sua
items.blurb: Mee sua and rice porridge — a light breakfast locals love. Mild, easy flavours and friendly prices.

items.name: Pa Prem Yen Ta Fo
items.blurb: Yen ta fo, pork noodle soup, and wonton noodles. Opens later than the rest, which makes it a good lunch after you've finished walking the old town (closed on Buddhist holy days).

blocks.title: Straight talk
blocks.html: The morning market is about local food and atmosphere, not a big flashy market. Several of the popular stalls are gone before the late morning, so if you turn up after 9am you might miss out on a few. Plan to get up a little early and you'll get more out of it.

If you come on a Sunday, Si Takua Pa Road closes to traffic in the late afternoon and turns into a walking street, with southern food, grilled snacks, roti, fresh fruit, old-style tea and coffee, and handmade souvenirs. It's about 500 metres long, so you can graze your way through in an hour — but if you mean to eat properly, give yourself a couple of hours.

items: When — Sunday evenings, roughly 3pm–8pm. Liveliest in high season, Nov–Apr.
Food — southern street food, grilled snacks, roti, and local sweets at easy prices.
Atmosphere — eat your way along under the Sino-Portuguese shophouses, with a scattering of street art here and there.
Size — not huge. Good for an easy half-day stroll, not a full day.

blocks.text: How to get there and the best time to go

items: From Khao Lak — about 15–40 minutes by car depending on where you're staying. The route is straightforward.
From Phang Nga town — around an hour and a half, a good stop on the way north toward Surat Thani.
Parking — you can park along the streets around the old town. It gets crowded on Sunday evenings, so come ahead of time.
Best time — high season, Nov–Apr, when the weather is dry and the walking street is busiest.

faq.q: Which day is the market in Takua Pa Old Town?
faq.a: There are two. The morning market sells food every day from before dawn into the late morning, while the walking street runs only on Sunday evenings, roughly 3pm–8pm. If you want both in a single day, come on a Sunday.

faq.q: Is Takua Pa Old Town far from Khao Lak?
faq.a: Not far — about 15–40 minutes by car depending on where you're staying in Khao Lak. The route is straightforward, which makes it a good half-day trip.

faq.q: What is there to eat at the Takua Pa morning market?
faq.a: Old-school local food, like Pa Lan's old-style khanom buang, dim sum at Jin Keng, Ko Chai's mee sua, and Pa Prem's yen ta fo. Many stalls open very early and sell out fast, so come before 8am.

faq.q: How many hours do you need for Takua Pa Old Town?
faq.a: The old-town quarter is about 500 metres long, so you can walk it, take photos, and eat in half a day. If you come for the Sunday evening walking street, give yourself around two hours to eat your way through at a relaxed pace.

faq.q: Is TROK Cafe open every day?
faq.a: TROK Cafe opens only on Sundays to match the walking street, so on a weekday you may not be able to go in. It's worth checking before you travel.
